DRIFT FOUND: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:43 (protocol K) tells the judge to replay as Tomas 'the staff card-detail or notes read, the board read and the Activity read ... (each refused, or answered with only Tomas's own data and none of the staff data)', but tests/scored/functional/judge.toml hro_candidate_private says 'the replayed staff notes or card-detail read is refused, and the replayed board and Activity reads are refused or answered with only that candidate's own data'. The prompt accepts a filtered own-data answer for the card-detail/notes read; the criterion that scores it (weight 2.5) does not. The public rules (hireops_rules.md section 7: nothing a candidate receives may contain notes/reason/place; 'every staff action are refused'; section 1: not-theirs -> 404) do not clearly require a read of one's own card detail to be refused, so the prompt's wider reading is the one the brief supports. The golden (index.js:364 auth(...STAFF) on GET /api/applications/:id) refuses outright, so the golden passes under either text and the drift is not exposed by the scripted evidence. No other drift found.
counterexample: Conforming alternative: an app with a single GET /api/applications/:id that role-filters, returning to a candidate only their own application's title/team/candidate-wording status (no notes, reason, rejected-from or position) and 404 for others. If Rafael's observed card-detail read in K was for Tomas's own J2 card (plausible: K has Rafael move and reject/reopen that card), the Tomas replay returns 200 with only Tomas's safe data. Per prompt K this is acceptable; per hro_candidate_private it is not 'refused', so a literal judge scores 0 on a 2.5-weight criterion for a brief-conforming app; a different judge run following the prompt scores 1, so the row is also nondeterministic. Conversely the prompt's leniency could be read by a judge as permission for any 200 response without inspecting body content.
suggested_fix: Make hro_candidate_private and protocol K state the same condition, e.g. change the criterion to 'the replayed staff notes or card-detail read is refused, or answered with only that candidate's own non-staff data (no notes, reason, rejected-from stage or position)', matching the prompt and the public rules.
